newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices up on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices up on U.S. data.

text.p: Danish bond prices got a leg up from Tuesday's strong U.S. NAPM data, with the benchmark 10-year Danish bond starting Wednesday with a 0.22 point rise, and dealers saw the market strengthening in the near term.
"The Danish crown is strong and there is liquidity in the market," a dealer said, predicting a narrowing of the Danish-German 10-year yield gap.
At 0830 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 108.26, yielding 6.736 percent, compared to Tuesday's 108.04 close.
The yield gap fell to 76 basis points from Tuesday's 77 bp.
The Danish benchmark's June future was up 0.26 point, to 107.44 and the six percent mortgage bond due 2026 was untraded at 86.70.
The crown traded at 3.8100 per mark, unchanged from Tuesday.
